ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Given two objects, A and B, with masses $m_{A}=2\mathrm{{kg}}$ and $m_{B}=1\mathrm{kg}$ respectively, object A is released from rest at a height $h=1.2m$ and falls freely, while object B is launched vertically upwards from the ground. After colliding at time $t=0.2\mathrm{s}$, the two objects stick together and move as a single mass. The acceleration due to gravity is given as $g=10m/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. Determine the height $x$ above the ground at which the collision occurs.
2. Determine the velocity $v$ after the collision.

3. Calculate the mechanical energy loss $\Delta E$ due to the collision.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Given two objects, A and B, with masses $m_{A}=2\mathrm{kg}$ and $m_{B}=1\mathrm{kg}$ respectively, object A is released from rest at a height $h=1.2\mathrm{m}$ and falls freely, while object B is launched vertically upwards from the ground. After colliding at time $t=0.2\mathrm{s}$, the two objects stick together and move as a single mass. The acceleration due to gravity is given as $g=10\mathrm{m/s}^{2}$. 1. Determine the height $x$ above the ground at which the collision occurs. 2. Determine the velocity $v$ after the collision. 3. Calculate the mechanical energy loss $\Delta E$ due to the collision.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Take upward as positive. The given quantities are m_A=2 kg, m_B=1 kg, h=1.2 m, t=0.2 s, and g=10 m/s^2. Object A is released from rest, so its collision height is x=h-(1/2)gt^2=1.2-(1/2)(10)(0.2)^2=1.2-0.2=1.0 m. Its velocity just before collision is v_A=-gt=-10(0.2)=-2 m/s. Object B starts from the ground and reaches the same height x at t=0.2 s, so x=u_B t-(1/2)gt^2. Thus 1.0=0.2u_B-0.2, giving u_B=6 m/s. Its velocity just before collision is v_B=u_B-gt=6-2=4 m/s. Because they stick together, use conservation of momentum during the collision: v=(m_A v_A+m_B v_B)/(m_A+m_B)=(2(-2)+1(4))/(3)=0 m/s. The kinetic energy just before collision is (1/2)(2)(2^2)+(1/2)(1)(4^2)=4+8=12 J, and after collision it is 0, so the mechanical energy loss is ΔE=12 J.
